text:
maya: seeing ~3% GPU launches in ap-south1 failing with `fsync timed out` on scratch volume. node logs show NVMe temp spikes and a controller reset. noticed after last janitor roll.
leo: can you paste the node logs?
maya: here are snippets from /var/log/kern.log on gnode-aps1-42:
```
Mar 10 03:12:11 kernel: nvme0: temperature above threshold: 95C
Mar 10 03:12:13 kernel: nvme nvme0: controller reset due to error
Mar 10 03:12:15 kernel: overlayfs: fsync failed on tmpfile: -110
Mar 10 03:12:16 kubelet[1234]: attach/detach for scratch-volume timed out
```
sam: those temps are brutal. are these preemptible/spot machines or dedicated?
dave-oncall: ap-south1 pool is a mix - GPU spot + fallback to reserved. i'm seeing scrub/cleaner cronjobs kick at 03:10 UTC which overlaps heavy batch window (03:00-03:30).
leo: i ran `iostat -x 1 3` while reproducing on a test node, output:
```
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s  rrqm/s wrqm/s r_await w_await  aqu-sz  svctm  %util
nvme0n1         150.00  1220.00  4800   61440   0.00  0.00   2.1    18.3    1.10   0.35   62.5
```
leo: high write bursts + long w_await -> queueing, NVMe controller heating -> thermal throttle -> firmware reset -> fsync stalls
maya: we also see janitor running with concurrency=8 in ap-south1. that likely spikes tiny-file deletes and causes write amplification on the scratch device.
sam: short-term mitigation idea: reduce janitor concurrency in ap-south1 to 1, and move cron to 04:30 (outside batch window). also throttle janitor with `ionice` or `rsync --bwlimit` style backoff where possible.
dave-oncall: agreed. downside: backlog of tmp files will increase and some hosts may run low on free space if we delay too long. cost/ops tradeoff: more ephemeral retention -> risk of out-of-disk vs immediate GPU launch failures.
maya: can we apply a targeted patch just for ap-south1 and keep other regions unchanged? prefer canary first.
leo: yes. patch I tested locally:
```
kubectl patch cronjob scratch-cleaner -n infra --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/concurrencyPolicy","value":"Forbid"},{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/schedule","value":"30 4 * * *"}]'
```
deploy-bot: Scheduling rollout: cronjob/scratch-cleaner -> namespace infra -> rollout id rb-705000.
infra-bot: Autoscaler: suspended 12 pending GPU pods in ap-south1 due to node transient Attach/Detach errors at 7050001152. Monitoring.
sam: how much extra scratch capacity do we need if we lower concurrency? rough estimate: 8% more retained files during daylight, maybe +5-10GB per node. cost negligible vs GPU failures.
dave-oncall: open INC: <https://r.issues/INC-7050|INC-7050> and tag storage+infra. i'll run node-level temp fencing to force evict before thermal threshold.
maya: pushing canary patch to ap-south1 now, will monitor for 30m. also enabling nvme soft-threshold at 85C to trigger proactive eviction (kernel flag set via sysfs on canary nodes).
leo: note: long-term we should add per-pool janitor rate-limiter and prefer deferred deletion via object store for large tmp churn workloads. also consider pre-warming larger scratch volumes for heavy batch windows.
sam: and we should add an alert for NVMe controller resets per-node so this is triaged earlier.
maya: canary applied. Observability links: perf dashboard -> <https://r.metrics/ap-south1/scratch-fsync|ap-south1 scratch fsync> (watching rv:fsync_time p95)
dave-oncall: i'll keep the incident open and watch GPU queue. thx all.
maya: update (7050001399): after lowering concurrency and moving cron, GPU launches dropped to baseline and no further controller resets observed on canary nodes. rolling to remaining ap-south1 hosts in 30m.
leo: follow-up action items: 1) implement per-region janitor rate-limit (github PR #1248), 2) add NVMe-reset alert, 3) run a wear-leveling audit for ap-south1 hardware batch.
maya: added PR link in INC-7050. closing thread for now. :thumbsup:
